# Proposal: Document behaviors shipped without a spec

## Why

Four behaviors reached `main` through ordinary pull requests: they are
implemented, tested and listed in the changelog, but no spec in
`_codev/specs/` describes them. The specs are authoritative, so a later
change could remove one of these behaviors without any requirement noticing.
This change brings the specs back in line with what codev already does. It
changes no behavior.

## What Changes

- **Decisions — Windows line endings**: specify that an ADR saved with CRLF
  line endings is parsed like its LF equivalent. Specify that the seal hashes
  the body byte for byte, with no line-ending normalization. Specify that
  rewriting an ADR's status keeps the file's line-ending style and does not
  change its sealed body.
- **Docs — warning callouts in the offline HTML**: specify that a blockquote
  opening on `**Warning**` or `**Attention**` is rendered as a warning
  callout, styled apart from other blockquotes. Every other blockquote stays
  a plain blockquote.
- **Docs — silent exit when the output is cut**: specify that
  `codev docs --print` piped into a reader that stops early (`head`) exits
  with code 0 and prints no error.
- **Init — forward slashes in inherited paths**: specify that every local
  path `codev init --inherit` writes into `config.yaml` uses forward slashes
  on every platform. Specify too that a git source given by a relative local
  path (`../shared.git@dev`) is written as an absolute path, like a relative
  local folder already is.

Assumptions made without asking (evaluation run, no user available):

- "The slashes in inheritance paths" means the forward-slash normalization
  of the paths that `codev init --inherit` writes, not the parsing of
  `--inherit` values. Parsing already covers trailing slashes and the
  `scheme://host/` split, and those parts of the spec are untouched.
- The absolute-path rule for relative local git sources is documented in
  the same requirement. It is the same unspecified behavior of the same
  code path, and slash normalization applies to it.
- "Silent exit when the doc display is cut" means the broken-pipe case of
  `codev docs --print`, the only form that writes the docs to a pipe.
- The seal's lack of CRLF normalization is documented as it is. Changing it
  would invalidate existing seals and is out of scope.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: ADRs saved with Windows line endings

An ADR whose lines end with CRLF (`\r\n`), as files saved on Windows do,
SHALL be read exactly like the same ADR with LF line endings: same
identifier, title, status, date, tags and sections, and no finding that the
LF version would not raise.

The seal SHALL hash the body as it is stored, byte for byte, with no
line-ending normalization. A CRLF body and its LF equivalent therefore have
different seals.

When the CLI rewrites the `status` of an existing ADR (accepting it, or
superseding it), it MUST keep the file's line-ending style: a CRLF file gets
a CRLF frontmatter back, with no mixed line endings. The body MUST stay
byte for byte identical, so its seal still matches.

#### Scenario: A CRLF ADR is parsed like an LF one

- **GIVEN** a well-formed ADR `0001` with LF line endings
- **AND** the same ADR with every `\n` replaced by `\r\n`
- **WHEN** the parser reads both files
- **THEN** both expose the identifier `0001`, the same title and the same
  status
- **AND** neither raises `decision_missing_frontmatter`

#### Scenario: A CRLF body is sealed as stored

- **GIVEN** an accepted ADR saved with CRLF line endings
- **WHEN** its seal is computed
- **THEN** the seal is the SHA-256 of the body bytes, `\r\n` included
- **AND** it differs from the seal of the same body with LF line endings

#### Scenario: Changing the status of a CRLF ADR keeps its sealed body

- **GIVEN** a proposed ADR `0001` saved with CRLF line endings
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev decision accept 0001`
- **THEN** the frontmatter reads `status: accepted` and its lines end with
  `\r\n`
- **AND** the body after the closing `---` is byte for byte unchanged
- **AND** the file contains no line ending that mixes `\n` and `\r\n`

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Warning callouts stand out in the offline HTML

In the HTML that `codev docs` generates, a blockquote whose first paragraph
opens with exactly the bold title `**Warning**` (English) or
`**Attention**` (French) SHALL be rendered as a warning callout. Its
background, its rule and its title color set it apart from other
blockquotes, in both light and dark color schemes, using the inline
stylesheet only. These are the same titles the documentation website
recognizes.

Every other blockquote, including one that opens with another bold title
such as `**Note**`, MUST stay a plain blockquote. The markdown printed by
`--print` is not affected.

#### Scenario: Warning and Attention blockquotes become callouts

- **GIVEN** documentation containing `> **Warning**` followed by text, and
  `> **Attention**` followed by text
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev docs --write out.html`
- **THEN** both blockquotes are rendered as warning callouts in `out.html`

#### Scenario: A note stays a plain blockquote

- **GIVEN** documentation containing `> **Note**` followed by text
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev docs --write out.html`
- **THEN** that blockquote is rendered as a plain blockquote, without the
  warning style

### Requirement: `codev docs --print` exits quietly when its reader stops early

When the reader of `codev docs --print` closes its end of the pipe before
the whole documentation is written, for example `codev docs --print | head`,
the command MUST exit with code 0 and MUST NOT print any error. A reader
that leaves early is not a failure.

#### Scenario: Piped into `head`

- **GIVEN** the current binary
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev docs --print | head -n 5`
- **THEN** the first five lines of the documentation are shown
- **AND** nothing is written to stderr
- **AND** `codev` exits with code 0

#### Scenario: Read in full

- **GIVEN** the current binary
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev docs --print | cat`
- **THEN** the whole documentation is shown
- **AND** `codev` exits with code 0

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: `codev init --inherit` declares inherited sources

`codev init` SHALL accept `--inherit <SOURCE>`, any number of times. A
SOURCE is a git source when it starts with `git@`, `https://`, `http://`,
`ssh://` or `file://`, or ends with `.git` once an optional `@<ref>`
suffix is removed; anything else is a local path. A git source MAY carry an
`@<ref>` suffix (`https://example.com/acme/conventions.git@v2`); the `@`
of a user name before the host (`git@github.com:…`) is not a ref
separator. Without a suffix the ref is `main`.

When `codev init` writes `_codev/config.yaml`, it MUST declare every
source under `inherits:`, in the order given, as `git:` + `ref:` or as
`path:`, with the comment `# set with codev init --inherit` above the
key. A relative local path MUST be written as an absolute path, so that it
resolves the same from any folder of the project. The same applies to a git
source given as a relative local path (`../shared.git@dev`): its `git:`
value MUST be written as an absolute path, since git would otherwise resolve
it against whatever folder it runs in. The written file MUST stay readable
by every other codev command.

Every path that `codev init` makes absolute MUST be written with forward
slashes (`/`) as separators, on every platform, Windows included. The file
then stays the same whatever machine ran `codev init`, and carries no
escaped backslashes. A local path given already absolute, or starting
with `~`, is written as given.

The command MUST refuse, before writing anything, with the stable code
`invalid_inherit`:

- an empty value;
- a git source with an empty ref (`…/conventions.git@`) or an empty URL;
- a local path that does not exist or is not a folder.

When `_codev/config.yaml` already exists, `codev init` MUST NOT modify it:
the sources are not written, and a warning with the code
`inherit_not_written` names them and tells the user to add them under
`inherits:` by hand.

No source is declared when `--inherit` is absent.

#### Scenario: A git source with a ref and a local path

- **GIVEN** a new project and an existing folder `/home/you/conventions`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev init --yes --inherit
  git@github.com:acme/conventions.git@v2 --inherit /home/you/conventions`
- **THEN** `_codev/config.yaml` contains, under `inherits:`, an entry
  `git: git@github.com:acme/conventions.git` with `ref: v2`, then an entry
  `path: /home/you/conventions`
- **AND** the line above `inherits:` reads
  `# set with codev init --inherit`
- **AND** `codev status` and `codev sources list` read the file without
  error

#### Scenario: A git source without a ref gets `main`

- **WHEN** the user runs `codev init --yes --inherit
  https://example.com/acme/conventions.git`
- **THEN** the declared source carries `ref: main`

#### Scenario: A relative path on Windows is written with forward slashes

- **GIVEN** a new project at `C:\work\app` on Windows
- **AND** an existing folder `C:\work\conventions`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev init --yes --inherit ..\conventions`
- **THEN** `_codev/config.yaml` declares a `path:` entry that names the
  absolute path of `C:\work\conventions` and contains only `/` as a
  separator, with no `\`
- **AND** `codev status` reads the file without error

#### Scenario: A relative local git repository is made absolute

- **GIVEN** a new project at `/home/you/app` and a local repository
  `/home/you/shared.git`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev init --yes --inherit ../shared.git@dev`
- **THEN** `_codev/config.yaml` declares `git: /home/you/shared.git` with
  `ref: dev`

#### Scenario: An absolute or `~` path is written as given

- **GIVEN** an existing folder `~/shared`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev init --yes --inherit ~/shared`
- **THEN** `_codev/config.yaml` declares `path: ~/shared`

#### Scenario: An invalid value is refused before anything is written

- **GIVEN** a folder without `_codev/`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev init --yes --inherit ./does-not-exist`
- **THEN** the command fails with the code `invalid_inherit`
- **AND** no file or folder has been created

#### Scenario: An existing configuration is left untouched

- **GIVEN** a project whose `_codev/config.yaml` already exists
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev init --yes --inherit /home/you/conventions`
- **THEN** `_codev/config.yaml` is identical byte for byte
- **AND** a warning `inherit_not_written` names the source
